steps.script: Stay with your crewmate. Shout their name and tap their shoulders. Do they respond?
Call out for the rest of the crew and press the emergency alarm. Tell me when that is done.
Check for breathing and feel for a pulse at the neck for no more than ten seconds. Is there normal breathing and a pulse?
Start chest compressions now, using the microgravity CPR method from your onboard medical checklist. Have another crew member bring the defibrillator. Tell me when the defibrillator is here.
Attach the defibrillator pads as shown on the pads. Turn it on and follow its voice prompts. Tell me when it starts analysing.
Did the defibrillator advise a shock?
Make sure everyone is clear of the crewmate and the restraints. Press the shock button when the defibrillator tells you. Then resume compressions straight away. Tell me when you have resumed.
No shock. Resume chest compressions straight away and follow the defibrillator prompts. Tell me when you have resumed.
Keep going for two minutes, or until the defibrillator asks you to stop. Now check: is the crewmate breathing normally and do they have a pulse?
Secure your crewmate so they cannot drift, keep their airway clear, and stay with them. Check breathing and pulse every minute. Tell me when they are secured.
Good. Ask your crewmate to stop all activity and secure them comfortably. Stay with them. Tell me when they are settled.
Ask them: are they short of breath, sweating heavily, or is the pain spreading to the arm, jaw or back?
Attach the ECG or cardiac monitor from the medical kit. Tell me when the trace is running.
Open the onboard cardiac emergency checklist and follow the medication step it lists. I cannot choose or dose medication for you. Tell me when you have finished that checklist step.

steps.checklist_label: Has the crewmate collapsed or stopped responding?
steps.script: Is your crewmate still awake and responding to you?

steps.checklist_label: Prepare packet for the flight surgeon
steps.script: I am preparing the incident packet for the flight surgeon with the latest vitals and the steps you have done. If you have a trained crew member, capture the guided cardiac ultrasound or ECG image and attach it. Tell me when you are ready to send.

The packet is ready. It will be sent to the flight surgeon, or queued for uplink if the signal delay is long. Stay with your crewmate and keep monitoring. This guidance is decision support only and does not replace your onboard medical procedures.
Protocol complete. Keep monitoring your crewmate until the flight surgeon responds.
